idea: A dormant card wakes up for a legitimate holiday trip with a new phone, an out-of-region billing code, and a high bank risk score, stacking B5_dormant + January score + vector_precedent to push a legitimate customer over the 0.70 block/report threshold.

case.trigger_text: High risk score (0.89) on online reservation purchase of $1,185.00 following extended card inactivity (dormant 45+ days) from unrecognised iOS device in region 384.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: B5_dormant fires with LR 5.65 on the waking dormant card, while the high online Product R purchase in a new region with a 0.89 risk_score matches the 24-dim vector profile of confirmed fraud (triggering similar_cases_vec LR 2.90). Combined, two independent measured detectors push fraud probability above 0.70/0.85 and exposure > $1,000, tricking Assay into recommending BLOCK_CARD and FILE_REPORT on an innocent traveller using their backup card.

idea: An office manager buys three small digital gift cards for employees and then a laptop on the company card in under an hour, mimicking the exact R5 card-testing signature (3 small online auths + 1 purchase > $100) to force an automatic BLOCK_CARD.

case.trigger_text: Velocity alert: 3 small online Product C authorizations ($10.00, $10.00, $15.00) within 45 minutes followed by a $649.99 online purchase. Risk score 0.74.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Because Assay switched off 'innocence' signals (B29_innocence.md), the home device, home P_email, and home billing region do not reduce the score. Meanwhile, the sequence of 3 small online charges followed by a cleared >$100 purchase within an hour matches the Round 1 pattern classifier and Policy Rule R5 (Card testing), causing Assay to recommend BLOCK_CARD on a legitimate customer buying New Year employee gift cards.

idea: Twelve legitimate customers in a neighbourhood HOA pay their annual $24.50 dues online to the treasurer's email (cox.net) and one customer forgets and disputes it, triggering both micro_drip_cohort and recipient fan-in plus dispute weight to file a false SAR and monitor 11 innocent neighbours.

case.trigger_text: Customer contacted support questioning an unfamiliar $24.50 online charge to recipient domain cox.net; customer states their spouse may have paid the annual community fee or the card may be compromised.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Look at HHF-004 and HHF-006 in Assay's ablation notes: 'Without the measured dispute weight, HHF-004 drops from fraud to uncertain' and 'Without micro_drip_cohort, HHF-004 loses its 16 linked cards and its report. A $23.99 loss that connects to other cards needs a report under 3a.' Here, a customer inquiry/report on a $24.50 charge combined with 12 cards paying the same recipient amount triggers both the dispute weight and the cohort/fan-in link, tricking Assay into judging a legitimate HOA fee as confirmed fraud, blocking Card A, and filing a regulatory SAR.

idea: An extended family of 7 cardholders sharing a single home desktop computer and billing region during a January clearance sale forms a tight 7-card component (under the 15-card ring cap) where one member makes a high-scored luxury purchase, triggering ring_wcc and CPC/shared-origin false positives.

case.trigger_text: High risk score (0.86) on $1,420.00 purchase; device profile Windows | Windows 10 | chrome 63.0 | 1920x1080 and email domain comcast.net observed across 7 distinct cards within 16 hours.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: The 7 family cards sharing a single desktop device, email domain, and region stay well underneath Assay's 15-card ring cap (B15_rings.md), while exhibiting high risk scores across multiple cards in a short window. If any card in the component overlaps with historical fraud or triggers burst_hub / cpc / ring_wcc alongside vector_precedent on the $1,420 purchase, Assay treats the household computer as a shared fraud origin under Rule R6 and blocks/reports an innocent family.
